prompt:
TASK:
            How do you use definite and indefinite forms of nouns in Swedish? Give simple examples.

            PREVIOUS BEST DRAFT (score: 3.2/5.0):
            ---
            Definite form: Man säger att "barnet" är bäst.
Indefinite form: Man säger att "ett barn" är bäst.
            ---

            REVISION INSTRUCTIONS:
            Rewrite the draft above to address the following issues.
            Preserve what was already working well. Do not simply patch — rewrite
            sections where issues are deep.


The following issues MUST be fixed in this revision:
  ✗ [FC-001] Factual Correctness: Incomplete explanation of Swedish definiteness and grammatical gender distinctions. (flagged 2 times)
  ✗ [CC-001] Clarity & Communication: Lack of context or explanation about grammatical rules governing definite and indefinite forms. (flagged 2 times)
  ✗ [DC-001] Depth & Completeness: Failure to explain how to use definite and indefinite forms of nouns in Swedish. (flagged 2 times)

            Produce the improved version now. Output only the revised text, no preamble.
generated_text:
Definite form: Man säger att "barnets" är bäst.
Indefinite form: Man säger att "ett barn" är bäst.

Definiteness in Swedish depends on grammatical gender. "Barnet" is the definite form for a male child, while "barnets" is the plural definite form. "Barn" is the indefinite form for a male child.
